rulings.model: IRS text says "Add lines 1a through 1h"; the restatement adds only line 1a and line 1e.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; the model says the restatement adds only lines 1a and 1e of "Add lines 1a through 1h". Lines 1b to 1d and 1f to 1h are refused: scope.other_income asks for "other earned income (Form 1040 lines 1b to 1d and 1f to 1h)", wages or tips not on a Form W-2, Medicaid waiver payments and adoption benefits, and f1040.line8 refuses on it ("Prepare the required unsupported income or return treatment", citing Form 1040 lines 8, 10, 13b, 16, 19-20 and 27-31). On every computed return those lines are zero, so the sum is Form 1040 line 1z. Same ruling as round 2.

rulings.restated: Enter the amount from eic helper "Earned income credit for Form 1040, line 27a (Worksheet A, line 6, or Worksheet B, line 11 for a filer who answered Yes to Step 5, question 2, when Steps 1 to 5 are passed; zero otherwise)".
rulings.model: The referenced eic.credit helper returns only Worksheet A line 6 or zero; IRS Step 5 question 2 says for self-employed "Skip question 3 and Step 6; go to Worksheet B," whose line 11 is the credit.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; the model says the eic.credit helper "returns only Worksheet A line 6 or zero". The restated label it quotes names both worksheets ("Worksheet A, line 6, or Worksheet B, line 11 for a filer who answered Yes to Step 5, question 2"), and the computation follows Worksheet B for those filers (eic.line1 is eic.wsb_6, and lines 2 to 6 serve as Worksheet B lines 7 to 11; round 2 F2, relabelled since). i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A: "Use this worksheet only if you answered 'No' to Step 5, question 2. Otherwise, use Worksheet B"; p. 48, Worksheet B, line 11.

rulings.restated: Enter the amount from eic helper "The instructions say to check the box on line 27c (a STOP that says so, or Worksheet A line 2 is zero); the filer's own choice not to claim the EIC is not asked".
rulings.model: IRS says "Check the box on line 27c if you do not want to claim the earned income credit or if you have been instructed..."; the restatement expressly does not ask the filer's own choice.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; the model says the filer's own choice not to claim the EIC is not asked. i1040gi p. 43, Line 27c: "Check the box on line 27c if you do not want to claim the earned income credit or if you have been instructed to check the box in the instructions for line 27a". The rendered English states the limit itself ("the filer's own choice not to claim the EIC is not asked"), and it is a recorded design limit (TASKS.md T-027: "the filer's own choice not to claim is not asked"). The computed part (the instructed STOPs) is not disputed. Same ruling as round 2.

rulings.restated: Enter the amount from s8812 line 27.
rulings.model: IRS says "If you do not want to claim the ACTC, check here"; the restatement only enters the amount from Schedule 8812 line 27 and omits that election.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; the model says the line omits the box "If you do not want to claim the ACTC, check here". Form 1040 (2025) p. 2, line 28: "Additional child tax credit (ACTC) from Schedule 8812. If you do not want to claim the ACTC, check here"; i1040gi p. 61, Line 28: "If you do not want to claim the additional child tax credit, check the box on line 28." The project has no line for the box and no question for the election, and unlike line 27c (TASKS.md T-027) no scope or register record covers it: every return claims the ACTC and the box prints unchecked. The project's amount is right for a filer who claims the credit; a filer who elects not to claim gets line 28 = Schedule 8812 line 27 instead of the box checked and no credit. Severity: a printed box on every return, and an amount (line 28, 32, 33, refund) only for a filer who would opt out. Finding F1 in f1040.findings.md.
